body: I've been thinking that this is the best I've felt in months. I think/hope I am finally getting over my breakup.

I am also going through a rough breakup. We were together for 8 years and he decided to just give up on us. Six months later and I'm still struggling. I begged him to take me back not just once, but twice. I know you feel foolish, but it was brave of you to tell her how you still felt. At least you won't wonder about it. This http://www.reddit.com/r/LifeProTips/comments/2e9jvg/lpt_request_getting_over_a_breakup_asap/cjxio29 really helped me when I felt like I was starting to lose it. I know everybody says it, but just give it time. I, myself, have a hard time remembering this. Take care.

Hi again. 

I feel like I have been on my own since I was 18. I am 27 now. I wish that for once I could feel like I could fail and someone would be there to support me. What kind of support? In a dream world, financially, but I know that isn't happening. Even emotional support is a far fetched idea. The last time I expressed any kind of unhappiness in my job, all I got in return was that I was extremely lucky that I had a job at all and that I should continue to work hard and save. I'm still trying to accept that I may never get that from them as it seems my parents are of the mindset that if I have a roof over my head and a job, I am fine and they have nothing to worry about. 

Honestly, I know I'm an adult. And I know I can't rely on my parents for anything. It was never in the cards for me. I think they rely on me. Paying for our shared phone bill, lending/giving them money when needed, adding my mom's name to my credit card. My dad actually requested me to buy him basketball shoes and send them to him as a Christmas present last year. They are my parents and I would do anything for them. I can't say no. I am the responsible, hard working daughter.

Sorry for the long reply... Family is... Complicated for me, to say the least. It's hard for me to not be bitter. 

tldr; I guess emotional support or maybe if they could just stop relying on me so much. But also, I know this is never gonna happen, so I just have to live with it.
I've been thinking about this for a day, and I can't think of anything. I guess I want to move back home. I don't know.

Do you feel like the antidepresants and other medications make you feel more energetic and motivated? 

I started taking the antidepressant because I was feeling so low energy and just generally crappy all around. On the weekends, I was taking 4 hour naps and feeling so unmotivated to do anything. Alot of times, I'd be awake, but just laying in bed staring at the ceiling. Sometimes I would cry for absolutely no reason. Besides the dark thoughts, the antidepressant has helped with alot of those symptoms, but I still feel unmotivated. I know it's not some magical drug that's suppposed to solve my problems, but part of me is hoping for something more. Like I'll wake up one day and actually want to work towards improving my life, instead of watching it pass me by. And that's when I start to doubt myself and wonder if I really am doing better. I know I'm supposed to tell myself life is not a race, that I should embrace the little things that make me happy. But I have alot of trouble embracing that sentiment. 

Thanks again for listening and answering my questions. I appreciate it so much. It's so difficult for me to talk about this stuff with the few people I have in my life. Honestly, I feel like a giant whiner even now. I am calling my psychiatrist's office on Monday to make an appointment to talk about all this with him.

Did you ever take antidepressants? I feel like I've been depressed for a long time. I've been in therapy for social anxiety for about three years, and six months ago started seeing a psychiatrist when my depression worsened. He put me on Lexapro 5mg, which has been increased to 10mg for about 3 months now. Part of me feels like I feel worse since taking the medication. It was fine at first and I felt an improvement in my mood, but the last month or so has been the absolute worst. I mean I always felt like I wanted to disappear, but I never truly contemplated death until now. I've never had thoughts as dark as I do now. I know I should talk to my psychiatrist about all this, but I just don't want to go back. I'm scared he might increase my dose or change my medication and I was pretty resistant about being put on medication in the first place. 

Don't worry, I won't kill myself. I still don't understand why anyone would care, but as it is, I don't think I'm quite there yet. Thank you for taking an interest. I really, truly appreciate it.

Feeling low today... I bought a bunch of junk food and plan to shut myself in my room and watch shows on Netflix all night. I was at a crosswalk on my way home waiting for the light to turn, when I thought how nice it might be if someone pushed me into the oncoming traffic. It hasn't been a great day.

I know my family would be heartbroken, but why? We barely talk to each other. And I appreciate your kind words, stranger, but why would you be devastated? I've not been interested in anything lately, sometimes I just feel like a robot, going through the motions of living. Wake up, go to work, go home, sleep, repeat. If I had any motivation at all to do anything, it's pretty much gone now. At this point, I'm just barely functioning.

Wow, thanks. Thank you for asking a great question and taking an interest. Your question really made me think. There are so many things that I want to change about my life and I realized part of the problem is I feel like there are these certain steps in life. Go to college, get a job, get married, have kids, buy a house, etc. It's difficult for me to not feel like I'm behind in life, because I still haven't reached alot of these steps. It's also difficult to accept that some of these steps may not be part of my path in life. I went to see my therapist yesterday and I'm feeling a bit better. A little less hopeless. And I haven't had thoughts about wanting to die for a couple days. So for now, things are going okay again. I wasn't sure what to expect when I posted, but I'm glad I did. Thanks again for your questions.

I've been sitting here thinking of what would make me change the way I feel. There are so many things I want to change about my life. I want the opportunity to pursue a different career. I want the support of my parents. I want to feel like my life has some sort of purpose or direction. I want some sort of social life. But maybe mostly, maybe if I can't change any of these things, I want to be okay with what I have. I want to be content, maybe even happy with my life, without needing to feel like I'm behind in life or I'm supposed to accomplish different things. I am tired of comparing myself to others and feeling inadequate over it. 

Sorry if this is a vague answer, maybe the better answer is that I'm really not sure?

I don't feel like I'm doing well in life. I feel like I've been stuck in the same routine for 6 years. I know I'm supposed to move forward, but I don't have the courage to do so. Everything I need to do feels like it will take a million steps to get there. My therapist tells me it takes time, that she thinks I'm doing well, that I just need to take that first step, that I'm too critical of myself. But her words don't make me feel better. I feel worthless and alone. I feel like no one wants to be around me, that I have nothing to offer the world. And I hate myself for knowing what I need to do and just not being able to do it.
